title.zh: 卷三十九 志第九: 地理志三
title.raw: 卷三十九 志第九: 地理志三 Volume 39 Treatises 9: Geography 3

translations.literal: Geography Treatise III: Zhongjing Circuit
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise III — Zhongjing Circuit

sentences.zh: 中京大定府，虞為營州，夏屬冀州，周在幽州之分。

translations.literal: Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture—in Yu's time it was Ying Prefecture; in Xia it belonged to Ji; in Zhou it lay within You's division.
translations.idiomatic: Dading Prefecture at Zhongjing had been Ying Prefecture under Yu, Ji territory under Xia, and part of You under Zhou.

translations.literal: Qin divided the realm into commanderies; this was Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin organized the empire into commanderies, the region became Liaoxi.

translations.literal: Under Han it was Xin'anping County.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it was Xin'anping County.

sentences.zh: 漢末步奚居之，幅員千里，多大山深谷，阻險足以自固。

translations.literal: At the end of Han the Bu Xi dwelt here; the domain ran a thousand li, with many great mountains and deep valleys—defiles enough to hold themselves secure.
translations.idiomatic: In late Han the Bu Xi occupied the land, a thousand-li tract of high mountains and deep valleys whose passes let them stand on their own.

sentences.zh: 魏武北征，縱兵大戰，降者一十餘萬，去之松漠。

translations.literal: Wei Wu-di on his northern campaign loosed troops in great battle; more than a hundred thousand surrendered and were sent away to Songmo.
translations.idiomatic: On his northern campaign Cao Cao fought a major engagement; over one hundred thousand men surrendered and were removed to Songmo.

sentences.zh: 其後拓拔氏乘遼建牙於此，當饒樂河水之南，溫渝河水之北。

translations.literal: Later the Tuoba clan, seizing the moment in Liaodong, set their headquarters here—south of the Raole River, north of the Wenyu River.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Tuoba, exploiting turmoil in Liaodong, pitched their headquarters here between the Raole and Wenyu rivers.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗伐高麗，駐蹕於此。

translations.literal: Tang Taizong campaigning against Goryeo halted his imperial progress here.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo and encamped here on imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 部帥蘇支從征有功，奚長可度率眾內附，為置饒樂都督府。

translations.literal: Division chief Su Zhi followed the campaign with merit; Xi chief Kedou led the masses to submit inward, and the Raole Protectorate was set up for them.
translations.idiomatic: Division chief Su Zhi distinguished himself on the campaign; Xi leader Kedou brought his people to submit, and the court established Raole Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 咸通以後，契丹始大，奚族不敢復抗。

translations.literal: After Xiantong the Khitan grew great and the Xi no longer dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantong era the Khitan rose in power and the Xi ceased to resist.

translations.literal: When the Founder established the state, the whole tribe became subjects.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu founded the dynasty, the entire tribe submitted.

sentences.zh: 聖宗嘗過七金山土河之濱，南望雲氣，有郛郭樓闕之狀，因議建都。

translations.literal: Shengzong once passed the bank of Qijin Mountain and the Tu River; gazing south at cloud vapors shaped like outer walls and towered gates, he discussed founding a capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong once traveled the Tu River below Qijin Mountain; seeing southern mists shaped like walls and gate-towers, he debated building a capital.

sentences.zh: 擇良工於燕、薊，董役二歲，郛郭、宮掖、樓閣、府庫、市肆廊廡，擬神都之制。

translations.literal: Skilled craftsmen were chosen from Yan and Ji; construction was supervised two years—outer walls, palace quarters, towers, treasuries, markets and colonnades modeled on the Divine Capital's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen from Yan and Ji were recruited; for two years they built walls, palaces, towers, storehouses, and market arcades on the model of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 統和二十四年，五帳院進故奚王牙帳地。

translations.literal: In Tonghe year 24 the Five Accounts Division presented the former Xi king's headquarters land.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 24 brought the Five Accounts Division's gift of the old Xi royal encampment grounds.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，城之，實以漢戶，號曰中京，府曰大定。

translations.literal: Year 25 the city was walled and filled with Han households; it was styled Zhongjing, the prefecture called Dading.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 the walls rose and Han households settled it; the capital was named Zhongjing and the prefecture Dading.

sentences.zh: 皇城中有祖廟，景宗、承天皇后御容殿。

translations.literal: Within the Imperial City were ancestral temples and portrait halls to Emperor Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial City held ancestral shrines and portrait halls for Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 城池湫濕，多鑿井泄之，人以不便。

translations.literal: The city moat was damp and low; many wells were dug to drain it—people found this inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The walled city sat in wet ground; numerous drainage wells were sunk, to the residents' inconvenience.

sentences.zh: 大同驛以待宋使，朝天館待新羅使，來賓館待夏使。

translations.literal: Datong Hostel received Song envoys; Chaotian Hall received Silla envoys; Laibin Hall received Xia envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong hostel lodged Song missions, Chaotian Hall Silla missions, and Laibin Hall Xia missions.

sentences.zh: 有七金山、馬盂山、雙山、松山、土河。

translations.literal: There were Qijin Mountain, Mayu Mountain, Twin Mountain, Song Mountain, and the Tu River.
translations.idiomatic: Landmarks included Qijin, Mayu, Twin, and Song mountains and the Tu River.

translations.literal: Ten prefectures, nine counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed ten prefectures and nine counties:

translations.literal: Dading County.
translations.idiomatic: Dading County.

translations.literal: Former Bai Xi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Bai Xi land.

translations.literal: Captive households from various states were settled here.
translations.idiomatic: Captives from many states were settled there.

translations.literal: Changxing County.
translations.idiomatic: Changxing County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Bincong County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Bincong County.

translations.literal: Various tribal peoples were settled here.
translations.idiomatic: Various tribal communities were placed there.

translations.literal: Fushu County.
translations.idiomatic: Fushu County.

sentences.zh: 本漢新安平地，開泰二年析京民置。

translations.literal: Originally Han Xin'anping territory; in Kaitai year 2 capital households were split off to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: It was Han Xin'anping land; Kaitai year 2 carved out capital residents to found the county.

translations.literal: Quannong County.
translations.idiomatic: Quannong County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Bincong County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Bincong County ground.

translations.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 detached capital households to create it.

translations.literal: Wending County.
translations.idiomatic: Wending County.

translations.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Kaitai year 2 from capital households.

translations.literal: Shengping County.
translations.idiomatic: Shengping County.

translations.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Founded in Kaitai year 2 from capital residents.

translations.literal: Guihua County.
translations.idiomatic: Guihua County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.

translations.literal: Shenshui County.
translations.idiomatic: Shenshui County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Tuhe County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Tuhe County ground.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Created in Kaitai year 2.

translations.literal: Jinyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyuan County.

translations.literal: Originally Tang Qingshan County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly within Tang Qingshan County.

translations.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 settled it with households drawn from the capital.

translations.literal: En Prefecture, Huaide Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: En Prefecture—Huaide Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Xin'anping County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Xin'anping County land.

translations.literal: Taizong established the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong created the prefecture.

translations.literal: In Kaitai times Bohai households filled it.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaitai Bohai households were settled there.

translations.literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, later to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: It first answered to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Enhua County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Enhua County.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai from Bohai households.
translations.idiomatic: Settled in Kaitai with Bohai households.

translations.literal: Hui Prefecture, Huihe Army, middle grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Prefecture—Huihe Army, middle grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Tang Guiyi Prefecture territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Guiyi Prefecture land.

sentences.zh: 太祖俘漢民數百戶兔鹿山下，創城居之，置州。

translations.literal: Taizu captured several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, founded a walled settlement, and set up the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, built a town, and established the prefecture.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing; governing one county: Huihe County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing; one county, Huihe County.

sentences.zh: 聖宗遷上京惠州民，括諸宮院落帳戶置。

translations.literal: Shengzong moved Hui Prefecture households from Shangjing and gathered palace and camp registered households to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong relocated Hui households from Shangjing and enrolled palace and camp registers to populate it.

translations.literal: Gao Prefecture, observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Prefecture (observation commissioner).

translations.literal: Tang Xin Prefecture territory.
translations.idiomatic: Former Tang Xin Prefecture land.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年，以契丹室活部置。

translations.literal: In Wansui Tongtian year 1 it was set up for the Khitan Shihuo division.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui Tongtian year 1 placed the Khitan Shihuo division here.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，以俘戶置高州。

translations.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and established Gao Prefecture with captives.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo campaign founded Gao Prefecture with war captives.

translations.literal: There are Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.
translations.idiomatic: It has Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

sentences.zh: 三韓縣，辰韓為扶餘，弁韓為新羅，馬韓為高麗。

translations.literal: Sanhan County—Chenhan was Fuyu, Bianhan Silla, Mahan Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhan County: Chenhan stood for Fuyu, Bianhan for Silla, Mahan for Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，俘三國之遺人置縣。

translations.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and settled remnant people of the three states in the county.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo war placed survivors of the three Han states in the county.

translations.literal: Households 5,000.
translations.idiomatic: 5,000 households.

translations.literal: Wu'an Prefecture, observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu'an Prefecture (observation commissioner).

translations.literal: Tang Wo Prefecture territory.
translations.idiomatic: Former Tang Wo Prefecture land.

sentences.zh: 太祖俘漢民居木葉山下，因建城以遷之，號杏堝新城。

translations.literal: Taizu settled captured Han households below Muye Mountain, built a city to move them, styled Apricot Ridge New City.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu placed Han captives below Muye Mountain, walled a new town called Apricot Ridge, and moved them in.

sentences.zh: 復以遼西戶益之，更曰新州。

translations.literal: Liaoxi households were added; it was renamed Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi households swelled it and the seat was renamed Xin Prefecture.

translations.literal: Tonghe year 8 received the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 gave it the present name.

translations.literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.
translations.idiomatic: It began with a prefect and was later promoted.

sentences.zh: 有黃柏嶺、裊羅水、個沒裏水。

translations.literal: There are Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.
translations.idiomatic: Features include Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Woye County.
translations.idiomatic: Woye County.

translations.literal: Li Prefecture, middle grade, observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Prefecture—middle grade, observation commissioner.

translations.literal: Originally Zhongjing Fusu County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhongjing's Fusu County.

sentences.zh: 統和二十六年置刺史州，開泰元年升。

translations.literal: Tonghe year 26 set up as a cishi prefecture; Kaitai year 1 promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 26 made it a prefecture with a cishi; Kaitai year 1 elevated it.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Fusu County.
translations.idiomatic: Fusu County.

sentences.zh: 唐末，契丹漸熾，役使奚人，遷居琵琶川。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang the Khitan grew strong, put the Xi to labor, and moved them to dwell on the Pipa River.
translations.idiomatic: Late Tang saw the Khitan wax powerful, conscript Xi labor, and resettle them on the Pipa River.

translations.literal: Established as a county in Tonghe year 4.
translations.idiomatic: Made a county in Tonghe year 4.

translations.literal: First subordinate to Zhangmin Palace, then reassigned to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: It first belonged to Zhangmin Palace, then to Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Later a prefecture was set up, still subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: A prefecture followed, still under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Yu Prefecture, Gaoping Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Prefecture—Gaoping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Linyu County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Linyu County land.

translations.literal: Later subordinate to Youbeiping Licheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later it fell under Youbeiping's Licheng County.

sentences.zh: 唐載初二年，析慎州置黎州，處靺鞨部落，後為奚人所據。

translations.literal: Tang Zai Chu year 2 split Shen Prefecture to set up Li Prefecture for Mohe tribes; later the Xi seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Zai Chu year 2 Li Prefecture was carved from Shen to settle Mohe tribes, until the Xi took it.

sentences.zh: 太宗南征，橫帳解裏以所俘鎮州民置州，開泰中沒入。

translations.literal: Taizong on the southern campaign: the Horizontal Account Jieli settled captured Zhen Prefecture households and founded the prefecture; in Kaitai it was absorbed and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On his southern campaign Taizong's Horizontal Account Jieli placed Zhen captives here; Kaitai absorbed and abolished the prefecture.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing two counties:
translations.idiomatic: Two counties:

translations.literal: Hezhong County.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong County.

translations.literal: Originally Xinli County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Xinli County land.

translations.literal: Yonghe County.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Changcheng County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Changcheng County ground.

translations.literal: Established in Tonghe year 22.
translations.idiomatic: Founded in Tonghe year 22.

translations.literal: Ze Prefecture, Guangji Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Prefecture—Guangji Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Tuyin County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Tuyin County land.

sentences.zh: 太祖俘蔚州民，立寨居之，采煉陷河銀冶。

translations.literal: Taizu captured Wei Prefecture households, set up a stockade, and mined and smelted Xianhe silver works.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took Wei Prefecture captives, founded a stockade, and worked the Xianhe silver mines.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Zhongjing regent's office.
translations.idiomatic: It answered to the Zhongjing regent.

translations.literal: Ze Prefecture was set up in Kaitai.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai established Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有松亭關、神山、九宮嶺、石子嶺、濼河、撒河。

translations.literal: There are Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong Ridge, Shizi Ridge, the Luo River, and the Sa River.
translations.idiomatic: Landmarks include Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong and Shizi ridges, the Luo River, and the Sa River.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing two counties:
translations.idiomatic: Two counties:

translations.literal: Shenshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Shenshan County.

translations.literal: Spirit Mountain lies to the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Mountain stands in the southwest.

translations.literal: Luanhe County.
translations.idiomatic: Luanhe County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Xuwu County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Xuwu County land.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongxing Palace.

translations.literal: Bei'an Prefecture, Xinghua Army, upper grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Bei'an Prefecture—Xinghua Army, upper grade, with a prefect.

sentences.zh: 本漢女祁縣地，屬上谷郡。

translations.literal: Originally Han Nuqi County territory, belonging to Shanggu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Nuqi County in Shanggu Commandery.

translations.literal: Under Jin it was seized by Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Jin times saw Feng Ba take it.

translations.literal: Under Tang it was western territory of the Xi princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Tang made it the Xi princely house's western domain.

translations.literal: Shengzong settled Han households to establish Bei'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong placed Han households and founded Bei'an Prefecture.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Xinghua County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Xinghua County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Qieju County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Qieju County land.

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture, Guangrun Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Prefecture—Guangrun Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

sentences.zh: 本中京之龍山縣，開泰中置州，仍屬中京。

translations.literal: Originally Longshan County of Zhongjing; the prefecture was set up in Kaitai and remained under Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: It was Zhongjing's Longshan County; Kaitai made it a prefecture still under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Longshan County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Longshan County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Jiaoli County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Jiaoli County ground.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Xijia Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it from Xijia Stockade.

translations.literal: Songshan Prefecture, Sheng'an territory, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan Prefecture—Sheng'an territory, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai.
translations.idiomatic: Created in Kaitai.

translations.literal: Abolished in Tonghe year 8, then restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 abolished it; later it was restored.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Songshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Wencheng County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Wencheng County land.

translations.literal: Bordering Songmo, a merchant crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: On the Songmo frontier, a hub of trade.

translations.literal: Established as a county in Kaitai year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Made a county in Kaitai year 2.

translations.literal: There is the Song Mountain stream.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Mountain river runs through it.

sentences.zh: 宋王曾《上契丹事》曰：出燕京北門，至望京館。

translations.literal: Song minister Wang Zeng's Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan says: leaving Yanjing's north gate, one reaches Wangjing Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: from Yanjing's north gate to Wangjing Hostel,

translations.literal: fifty li to Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: fifty li to Shun Prefecture;

translations.literal: seventy li to Tan Prefecture, gradually entering mountains.
translations.idiomatic: seventy li to Tan Prefecture as the road climbs into hills;

translations.literal: fifty li to Jingou Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: another fifty li reaches Jingou Hostel.

sentences.zh: 將至館，川原平曠，謂之金溝澱。

translations.literal: Approaching the hostel, the river plain opens wide—called the Jingou shoals.
translations.idiomatic: Near the hostel the valley floor widens into what they call the Jingou flats.

sentences.zh: 自此入山，詰曲登陟，無復裏堠，但以馬行記日，約其里數。

translations.literal: From here one enters the mountains, winding up steep paths; there are no more mile markers—only days on horseback estimate the distance.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond lies twisting mountain grades without mileposts; travelers count days on horseback to reckon distance.

sentences.zh: 九十里至古北口，兩傍峻崖，僅容車軌。

translations.literal: Ninety li to Gubeikou; steep cliffs on both sides barely admit a cart track.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety li brings Gubeikou, where cliffs on both sides admit only a single cart track.

sentences.zh: 又度德勝嶺，盤道數層，俗名思鄉嶺，八十里至新館。

translations.literal: Crossing Desheng Ridge with its layered switchbacks—folk name Homesick Ridge—eighty li to Xin Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng Ridge's switchbacks, known as Homesick Ridge, lead eighty li to Xin Hostel.

sentences.zh: 過雕窠嶺、偏槍嶺，四十里至臥如來館。

translations.literal: Passing Diaoke Ridge and Pianqiang Ridge, forty li to Wolai Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Past Diaoke and Pianqiang ridges, forty li to the Reclining Tathagata Hostel.

sentences.zh: 過烏灤河，東有灤州，又過摸鬥嶺，一名渡雲嶺，芹菜嶺，七十里至柳河館。

translations.literal: Crossing the Wuluan River—with Luan Prefecture to the east—then Modou Ridge, also called Duyun Ridge and Qincai Ridge; seventy li to Liuhe Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuluan River is crossed with Luan Prefecture eastward; Modou Ridge, alias Duyun and Qincai ridges, lies seventy li before Liuhe Hostel.

sentences.zh: 松亭嶺甚險峻，七十里至打造部落館。

translations.literal: Songting Ridge is very precipitous; seventy li to the Forging Tribes Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Songting Ridge is sheer; seventy li farther stands the Forging Tribes Hostel.

sentences.zh: 東南行五十里至牛山館。

translations.literal: Southeast fifty li to Niushan Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li southeast to Niushan Hostel.

translations.literal: Eighty li to Lu'er Gorge Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li to Deer Gorge Hostel.

sentences.zh: 過蝦蟆嶺，九十里至鐵漿館。

translations.literal: Crossing Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Tiejiang Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Over Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Iron-Slurry Hostel.

sentences.zh: 過石子嶺，自此漸出山，七十里至富谷館。

translations.literal: Crossing Shizi Ridge, from here gradually leaving the mountains, seventy li to Fugu Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Shizi Ridge passed, the road slowly descends from the hills; seventy li to Fugu Hostel.

sentences.zh: 八十里至通天館，二十里至中京大定府。

translations.literal: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, twenty li to Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, then twenty li to Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城垣卑小，方圓才四里許。

translations.literal: The walls are low and small; the circuit barely four li square.
translations.idiomatic: Walls are low and the city circuit scarcely four li around.

translations.literal: Gates are only layered roofs, without tower-gate construction.
translations.idiomatic: Gatehouses are stacked roofs without barbican towers.

sentences.zh: 南門曰朱夏，門內通步廊，多坊門。

translations.literal: The south gate is called Zhuxia; within the gate connected walking corridors and many ward gates.
translations.idiomatic: The south gate Zhuxia opens on covered walkways and many lane gates.

sentences.zh: 又有市樓四：曰天方、大衢、通阛、望闕。

translations.literal: There are also four market towers: called Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.
translations.idiomatic: Four market towers stand: Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.

translations.literal: Next one reaches Datong Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Farther on lies Datong Hostel.

translations.literal: Its gate due north is called Yangde and Changge.
translations.idiomatic: Its north-facing gate bears the names Yangde and Changge.

translations.literal: Within the city on a hillock in the southwest corner is a temple.
translations.idiomatic: A temple crowns a southwest hill inside the walls.

translations.literal: South of the city are gardens, a place for banquets and archery.
translations.idiomatic: South of the walls lie gardens used for feasts and archery.

sentences.zh: 自過古北口，居人草庵板屋，耕種，但無桑柘；

translations.literal: From passing Gubeikou, inhabitants live in thatched huts and plank houses and farm, but there is no mulberry or catalpa;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Gubeikou people dwell in thatch huts and plank houses and till fields, yet plant no mulberry or catalpa;

sentences.zh: 所種皆從壟上，虞吹沙所壅。

translations.literal: all planting is on ridge crests, lest blown sand bury the crops.
translations.idiomatic: crops are sown on ridge tops for fear windblown sand would bury them.

sentences.zh: 山中長松郁然，深谷中時見畜牧牛馬橐駝，多青羊黃豕。

translations.literal: In the mountains tall pines grow dense; deep valleys sometimes show pastured cattle, horses, and camels—many blue sheep and yellow swine.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains hold thick pine; valleys often show cattle, horses, and camels, with many blue sheep and yellow hogs.

translations.literal: Cheng Prefecture, Xingfu Army, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Prefecture—Xingfu Army, military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉國長公主以媵戶置，軍曰長慶，隸上京。

translations.literal: The Jin state's Senior Princess established it with dowry households; the army was called Changqing, subordinate to Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Senior Princess founded it with dowry households under the Changqing army, subordinate to Shangjing.

translations.literal: The army name was changed again.
translations.idiomatic: The army designation was later renamed.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Tongchang County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Tongchang County.

translations.literal: Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhong Prefecture.

translations.literal: Originally Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army), military commissioner.

translations.literal: The ancient Guzhu state.
translations.idiomatic: Land of ancient Guzhu.

translations.literal: Han Liucheng County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Han Liucheng County ground.

sentences.zh: 慕容皝以柳城之北，龍山之南，福德之地，乃築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣，遂遷都，號曰和龍宮。

translations.literal: Murong Huang, taking the land north of Liucheng and south of Long Mountain as a place of fortune and virtue, built Long City, erected palaces and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng County, moved the capital, and styled it Helong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang deemed the tract between Liucheng and Long Mountain auspicious, built Long City with palaces and shrines, renamed Liucheng Longcheng County, moved the capital, and called it Helong Palace.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂復居焉，後為北跋所滅。

translations.literal: Murong Chui dwelt there again; later it was destroyed by Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui returned there; Northern Yan later destroyed it.

translations.literal: Northern Wei took it as Liaoxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made it Liaoxi Commandery.

translations.literal: Sui pacified Gao Baoning and set up Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sui subdued Gao Baoning and established Ying Prefecture.

translations.literal: Emperor Yang abolished the prefecture and set up Liucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Yang-di abolished the prefecture for Liucheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐武德初改營州總管府，尋為都督府。

translations.literal: Early Tang Wude changed it to Ying Prefecture chief commandery, soon a protectorate headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang Wude made it Ying chief command, soon a protectorate seat.

translations.literal: In Wansui Tongtian it fell to Li Wanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui Tongtian saw it lost to Li Wanrong.

translations.literal: Early Shenlong moved the headquarters to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shenlong shifted the seat to Youzhou.

translations.literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored administration at Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 4 returned government to Liucheng.

translations.literal: Year 8 it moved west to Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8 the seat moved west to Yuyang.

translations.literal: Year 10 it returned to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10 brought it back to Liucheng.

translations.literal: Later the Xi seized it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi later held it.

sentences.zh: 太祖平奚及俘燕民，將建城，命韓知方擇其處。

translations.literal: Taizu pacified the Xi and captured Yan households; intending to build a city, he ordered Han Zhifang to choose the site.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu subdued the Xi, took Yan captives, and charged Han Zhifang to choose a city site.

sentences.zh: 乃完葺柳城，號霸州彰武軍，節度。

translations.literal: Liucheng was then repaired and styled Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Liucheng was rebuilt as Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army) with a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 統和中，制置建、霸、宜、錦、白川等五州。

translations.literal: In Tonghe times the frontier commission of Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan five prefectures was set up.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe created a frontier commission over Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan prefectures.

translations.literal: Soon the commission was abolished; it was subordinate to Jiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The commission was soon dropped and the seat joined Jiqing Palace.

translations.literal: Later it belonged to Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later it passed to Xingsheng Palace.

translations.literal: Chongxi year 10 it was promoted to Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi year 10 elevated it to Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有大華山、小華山、香高山、麝香崖，天授皇帝刻石在焉，駐龍峪、神射泉、小靈河。

translations.literal: There are Great Huashan, Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk-fragrance Cliff—with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's carved stone—Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.
translations.idiomatic: It boasts Great and Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk Cliff with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's inscription, Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.

translations.literal: Two prefectures, four counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed two prefectures and four counties:

translations.literal: Xingzhong County.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhong County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.

sentences.zh: 太祖掠漢民居此，建霸城縣。

translations.literal: Taizu plundered Han households to dwell here and built Bacheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu settled plundered Han households and founded Bacheng County.

translations.literal: In Chongxi the prefecture was set up and the name changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi established the prefecture and renamed the county.

translations.literal: Yingqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqiu County.

translations.literal: Split off from Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Carved from Bacheng.

translations.literal: Xianglei County.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglei County.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Maiwu River.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it on the Maiwu River.

translations.literal: First subordinate to Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: First under Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Later subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Later subordinate.

translations.literal: Lüshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Lüshan County.

translations.literal: Originally Han Qielü County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Qielü County.

translations.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from the Luo Family Army.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 created it from the Luo Family Army.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing, later subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: First under Zhongjing, later under the prefecture.

translations.literal: An'de Prefecture, Huaping Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: An'de Prefecture—Huaping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Set up from Ba Prefecture's An'de County; came under this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Created from Ba's An'de County and attached here.

translations.literal: Governing one county: An'de County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: An'de County.

sentences.zh: 統和八年析霸城東南龍山徒河境戶置。

translations.literal: Tonghe year 8 split households from southeast Bacheng, Long Mountain, and Tuhe borders to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 settled households from southeast Bacheng and the Long Mountain and Tuhe marches.

sentences.zh: 初隸乾州，更屬霸州，置州來屬。

translations.literal: First subordinate to Qian Prefecture, then to Ba Prefecture; when the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.
translations.idiomatic: It first belonged to Qian, then Ba; establishing the prefecture brought it here.

translations.literal: Qian Prefecture, Fuchang Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Prefecture—Fuchang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Liaoxi Commandery territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Liaoxi Commandery land.

sentences.zh: 太祖平渤海，以所俘戶居之，隸黑水河提轄司。

translations.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and settled captives here, subordinate to the Blackwater River commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu conquered Bohai, placed captives here under the Blackwater River commissioner.

sentences.zh: 安帝置州，析宜、霸二州漢戶益之。

translations.literal: Emperor An established the prefecture and added Han households split from Yi and Ba prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An founded the prefecture and augmented it with Han households from Yi and Ba.

sentences.zh: 初隸永興宮，更隸中京，後置府，來屬。

translations.literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing; after the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.
translations.idiomatic: It passed from Yongxing Palace to Zhongjing, then to Xingzhong when that prefecture rose.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Shengji County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Shengji County.

sentences.zh: 太祖平渤海，俘興州盛吉縣民來居，因置縣。

translations.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai; captives from Xing Prefecture's Shengji County were settled here and the county established.
translations.idiomatic: After Bohai's conquest, Xing Prefecture's Shengji captives were settled and the county founded.

translations.literal: Yi Prefecture, Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Prefecture—Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commissioner.

translations.literal: Originally Liaoxi Lei County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Liaoxi Lei County land.

translations.literal: The Dongdan king hunted here every autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongdan king autumn-hunted here each year.

translations.literal: Xingzong established the prefecture with captives from Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong founded it with Ding Prefecture captives.

sentences.zh: 有墳山，松柏連亙百餘里，禁樵采，浚河，累石為堤。

translations.literal: There is Tomb Mountain; pines and cypresses run more than a hundred li; fuel cutting is forbidden; the river was dredged and stones piled for dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb Mountain bears pines and cypress for a hundred li with logging banned; the river was dredged and stone dikes raised.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Jiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiqing Palace.

translations.literal: Governing two counties:
translations.idiomatic: Two counties:

translations.literal: Hongzheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng County.

translations.literal: Shizong established it with Ding Prefecture captives.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong settled it with Ding captives.

translations.literal: Han laborers weave cloth; many are skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Han craftsmen weave cloth with notable skill.

translations.literal: Wenyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi County.

translations.literal: Established by Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong founded it.

translations.literal: First subordinate to Haibei Prefecture, later came under this seat.
translations.idiomatic: It first belonged to Haibei Prefecture, then to Yi.

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture, Linhai Army, middle grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Prefecture—Linhai Army, middle grade, military commissioner.

translations.literal: Originally Han Liaodong Wulü County.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Liaodong Wulü County.

translations.literal: Murong Huang set up Xile County.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang established Xile County.

translations.literal: Taizu established the prefecture with Han captives.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu founded the prefecture with Han captives.

sentences.zh: 有大胡僧山、小胡僧山、大查牙山、小查牙山、淘河島。

translations.literal: There are Great Huseng Mountain, Little Huseng Mountain, Great Chaya Mountain, Little Chaya Mountain, and Taohe Island.
translations.idiomatic: Landmarks include Great and Little Huseng and Chaya mountains and Taohe Island.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongyi Palace.

translations.literal: One prefecture, two counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed one prefecture and two counties:

translations.literal: Yongle County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle County.

translations.literal: Anchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Anchang County.

translations.literal: Yan Prefecture, Baosu Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture—Baosu Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Haiyang County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Haiyang County land.

sentences.zh: 太祖平渤海，遷漢戶雜居興州境，聖宗於此建城焉。

translations.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and moved Han households to mix in Xing Prefecture territory; Shengzong built a city here.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu after conquering Bohai mingled Han households in Xing Prefecture; Shengzong walled a city here.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace; came under this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongyi Palace, then attached to Jin Prefecture.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Xingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Xingcheng County.

translations.literal: Chuan Prefecture, Changning Army, middle grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Prefecture—Changning Army, middle grade, military commissioner.

translations.literal: Originally Tang Qingshan Prefecture territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Qingshan Prefecture land.

translations.literal: Taizu's younger brother Prince Ming Wang Anduan established it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's brother Prince Ming, Anduan, founded it.

translations.literal: Huitong year 3 an edict styled it Baichuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huitong year 3 renamed it Baichuan Prefecture by edict.

sentences.zh: 安端子察割以大逆誅，沒入，省曰川州。

translations.literal: Anduan's son Chalie was executed for great treason; the land was confiscated and abbreviated to Chuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Anduan's son Chalie died for treason; the domain was seized and the seat shortened to Chuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初隸崇德宮，統和中屬文忠王府。

translations.literal: First subordinate to Chongde Palace; in Tonghe it belonged to the Wenzhong princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: It first answered to Chongde Palace; Tonghe placed it under the Wenzhong princely house.

translations.literal: Governing three counties:
translations.idiomatic: Three counties:

translations.literal: Hongli County.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli County.

sentences.zh: 統和八年以諸宮提轄司戶置。

translations.literal: Tonghe year 8 established it with households from various palace commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 settled it with households from palace commissioners.

translations.literal: Xiankang County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang County.

translations.literal: Yimin County.
translations.idiomatic: Yimin County.

translations.literal: Established in Tonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Founded in Tonghe.

translations.literal: Yongba County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongba County.

translations.literal: Yongkang County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang County.

translations.literal: Originally Tang Changli County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Changli County land.

translations.literal: Lai Prefecture, Guide Army, lower grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Prefecture—Guide Army, lower grade, military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聖宗以女直五部歲饑來歸，置州居之。

translations.literal: Shengzong, when the five Jurchen divisions came in famine, settled them and set up the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong received the five Jurchen divisions in famine years and founded the prefecture to house them.

translations.literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.
translations.idiomatic: It began with a prefect and was later elevated.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongxing Palace.

sentences.zh: 有三州山、六州山、五脂山。

translations.literal: There are Sanzhou Mountain, Liuzhou Mountain, and Wuzhi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: It has Sanzhou, Liuzhou, and Wuzhi mountains.

translations.literal: Two prefectures, one county: Laibin County.
translations.idiomatic: It governed two prefectures and one county, Laibin County.

translations.literal: Originally Tang Laiyuan County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Laiyuan County land.

translations.literal: Xi Prefecture, Pinghai Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Prefecture—Pinghai Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Murong Huang set up Jining County.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang established Jining County.

sentences.zh: 聖宗括帳戶遷信州，大雪不能進，建城於此，置焉。

translations.literal: Shengzong gathered registered households to move to Xin Prefecture; heavy snow blocked the way, so a city was built here and the prefecture set up.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong mustered registers to relocate to Xin Prefecture; snow halted the march, so a city and prefecture were founded here.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Xingsheng Palace; came under this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xingsheng Palace, then attached to Xingzhong.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Haibin County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Haibin County.

translations.literal: Originally a Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a Han county.

sentences.zh: 瀕海，地多堿鹵，置鹽場於此。

translations.literal: Coastal; the ground is much alkaline salt; salt works were set up here.
translations.idiomatic: It borders the sea on saline soil where salt pans were established.

translations.literal: Qian Prefecture, Xingshan Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Prefecture—Xingshan Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

translations.literal: Originally Han Yangle County territory.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Yangle County land.

sentences.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷歸州民置，來屬。

translations.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Gui Prefecture households here; came under this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Da Yanlin, Shengzong resettled Gui Prefecture people here and attached the seat.

translations.literal: There is Jianjian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: It has Jianjian Mountain.

translations.literal: Governing one county: Qianmin County.
translations.idiomatic: One county: Qianmin County.

translations.literal: Run Prefecture, Haiyang Army, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Run Prefecture—Haiyang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

sentences.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷寧州之民居此，置州。

translations.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Ning Prefecture households here and set up the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Da Yanlin's defeat Shengzong relocated Ning Prefecture households and founded Run Prefecture.

translations.literal: Governing one county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Haiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang County.

sentences.zh: 本漢陽樂縣地，遷潤州，本東京城內渤海民戶，因叛，移於此。

translations.literal: Originally Han Yangle County territory; moved to Run Prefecture—originally Bohai households within the Eastern Capital inner city, relocated here because of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Yangle County; Run Prefecture received Eastern Capital Bohai households moved here after a revolt.
